## TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) can be associated with either staphylococci or
streptococci. Antimicrobial treatment and supportive care is urgent. Click one
of the links below for diagnostic criteria.
[Link to Diagnosis of Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome](orzid2-gmenu-strep-toxic-shock-syndrome)
[Link to Diagnosis of Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome](orzid2-gmenu-staph-toxic-shock-syndrome)
## _________________________________________________
## Treatment of Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome
## _________________________________________________
## Preferred treatment
Penicillin 4 million units IV q4h ($) [R] <AND> clindamycin 900 mg
IV q8h ($$) [H,O]
## Alternative for penicillin allergy
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV
q8h ($$) [H,O]
## _________________________________________________
## Treatment of Staphylococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome
## _________________________________________________
Use vancomycin initially in case methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is
present. If cultures reveal methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
(MSSA), change to nafcillin or cefazolin for better antimicrobial activity.
## Empirical treatment
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]
## Treatment if MSSA is isolated
Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) [H,O]) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$
Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) [R] <AND> Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h ($$) [H,O]
